summary: Makoto Yoshimura works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his doctoral studies at Waseda University around 1996–2002 and served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University around 2007.

Malcolm David Eckel studied at Oxford and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. A scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religion, he held posts at Middlebury, Harvard Divinity School, and Boston University (1990–2024), along with visiting professorships at Michigan and Sydney.

Mallica Kumbera Landrus works in Indology and history/archaeology. As of 2026, she is Keeper of Eastern Art at the Ashmolean Museum of Art and Archaeology and Associate Professor of Indian Art at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College.
Mamata Dash is an Indologist who completed her education at Ravenshaw Girls' School and Utkal University.

Mamoru Tonami was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology who earned his doctorate from Kyoto University. He taught at Kobe University and held successive posts at Kyoto University from 1965 to 2001, later serving as professor at Otani University in 2003.
Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist. He served as Secretary of The Asiatic Society and was DSA Sanskrit Co-ordinator at Jadavpur University, attested in 2003.

Manabu Asano works in Buddhist studies. He was a PhD student at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2020) and is attested as a researcher at Minobusan University in 2026.

Manasi Dilip Nadkarni specializes in linguistics and Indology. She conducted doctoral studies under Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and is attested as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

Manfred B. Steger studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and Rutgers University under Robert Baker Aitken. His career includes posts at Illinois State University, RMIT University, the University of Hawaiʻi, and Western Sydney University.

Manfred Mayrhofer was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Wilhelm Brandenstein at the University of Graz and held professorships at Saarland University (1962–1966) and the University of Vienna (1966–1990).

Manfred Taube was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Friedrich Weller at the University of Leipzig, where he became Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology in 1991.
Mannudeva was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Bālakṛṣṇa Pāyaguṇḍa (Bala Sharman Payagunde).

Manshi Kiyozawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Ernest Fenollosa and Mokurai Takeda at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University. He taught at Toyo University and became the founding president of Otani University in 1901.
Manu Leumann was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Munich (~1922–1927) and the University of Zurich (~1927–1959).

Marc Aurel Stein studied under Rudolf von Roth at Tübingen. An expert in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held leadership roles at Oriental College, Aliah University, Peshawar Museum, and the Archaeological Survey of India.
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Lausanne in 2016 under the supervision of Johannes Bronkhorst, having also studied under Nahid Rouzbeh.

Marc-Henri Deroche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Matthew T. Kapstein and was also taught by Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.
Marcel Cohen was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. He served on the faculties of the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1919–1954) and the University of Paris (1920–1954).

Marcel Granet studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes. A scholar of sinology and religious studies, he held professorships at EPHE, INALCO, and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises, which he founded.
Marcel Griaule studied at INALCO and EPHE under Marcel Mauss and Marcel Cohen. He later held an academic post at the University of Paris from 1942 to 1956.
